reason: A twenty-person research lab spending its round on compute: an honest 51/100. Recursive Superintelligence was incorporated in London, keeps offices in London and San Francisco, and is led by CEO and co-founder Richard Socher, formerly Chief Scientist at Salesforce, with a founding group that includes Tim Rocktäschel (UCL professor, ex-Google DeepMind), Jeff Clune, Josh Tobin (co-founder and CTO) and Tim Shi. It emerged from stealth on 13 May 2026 with $650 million at a $4.65 billion valuation, led by GV and Greycroft with AMD Ventures and Nvidia participating (SiliconANGLE, Tech.eu, TechFundingNews, 13 May 2026). The one event inside the 90-day window is not a capital event but a cost: on 28 July 2026 it signed a multi-year $410 million collaboration with AWS to run its automated AI-research system on Amazon's cloud (AWS press release; TechCrunch, 28 July 2026). That commits most of the round to compute before any product exists. The company describes a roughly twenty-person team, has no customers or revenue, and has said only that a 'Level 1' autonomous training demonstration and the earliest product examples should arrive before the end of 2026 (TechCrunch). No chief marketing officer, commercial lead or partnerships function has been announced, and no leadership tie to F1 or Formula E was found for any founder. Scored honestly: timing 12 (the AWS deal at 44 days; the round at 120 days is outside the window), capacity 18 ($650 million raised, $410 million of it now spoken for), brand fit 7 (a research lab with nothing to market yet), urgency 6 (a year-end demo, no launch or listing), operational fit 8 (automated research systems have no workstream a race team would deploy today). Total 51, below the 70 threshold. Not pitched. Re-run when the Level 1 system is public or when Recursive raises again with a commercial function in place; a London-incorporated lab at that point would be a natural London E-Prix conversation.
